title: Communications — Datalink — Relocate the Router to a Ventilated Shelf and Install the Cooling Duct
abstract: Moves the air traffic control datalink router two positions outboard into the main cooling flow, adds an inlet duct and a shelf temperature sensor, and puts the display interface unit in the vacated position.

sections.planning_reason: Ninety-four datalink unavailability events were recorded across the fleet in twenty-two months, half of them in the Gulf and southern Asia, and every one was accompanied by an over-temperature report from the router. Seventeen removed units tested serviceable in the shop. The router occupies a rack position selected for cable length rather than airflow, immediately behind a unit that runs warm. Operators are carrying no-fault-found removals and losing the operational benefit of the equipment on exactly the sectors where it matters most.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives the instructions to move the datalink router two positions outboard in the upper avionics rack, to install a ventilated mounting tray and a dedicated inlet duct at the shelf face, and to move the display interface unit into the vacated position. A shelf temperature sensor is added so that a rising temperature is reported as a maintenance message before the unit degrades. The coaxial run to the antenna is lengthened and re-clamped. The router itself, its software and the antenna installation are unchanged.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove electrical power from the aircraft and open the upper avionics compartment. Remove the datalink router and the display interface unit from the rack, using AMM-T-23-70-11-000-002-A. Remove the existing mounting trays. Install the ventilated tray at the outboard position and the inlet duct at the shelf face. Install the shelf temperature sensor and route its harness to the spare rack input. Install the router on the ventilated tray and the display interface unit in the vacated position using AMM-T-23-70-11-400-002-A. Fit the lengthened coaxial run and re-clamp it at the intervals given in the installation drawing. Re-terminate the two rack connections. Restore power and do the datalink functional test and the shelf sensor check. Close the compartment. Record the modification and update the configuration record.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft in the MSN T00020 to T00198 range. Aircraft delivered from MSN T00201 have the ventilated shelf from the production line and are outside the effectivity. The bulletin applies regardless of which cabin connectivity installation is fitted.
sections.material_note: Kit K2370-1014-01 covers one aircraft and has been available since June 2022. The ventilated tray and the duct are made to order with a sixteen week lead time. The removed trays are scrapped locally and are not returned.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled avionics compartment access, or within 30 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

issue.reason: Effectivity extended to the post cut-in aircraft whose upper rack loading was found to reproduce the unventilated condition; the accomplishment instructions are unchanged.
